script.introduction:
I teach blindfold chess here.
Blindfold chess is chess played without looking at the board — only the board in your head.
script.confidenceCheck: First, tell me: how well do you play right now?
script.choiceWithBoard: I can play with a board
script.confident:
Oh… impressive.
Then let's play a game right away.
script.chessPlayer:
If you know chess, this will be quick.
The first step in blindfold chess is knowing every square by name.
script.beginner:
Don't worry — everyone starts as a beginner.
Let's begin by learning the names of the squares.
script.readyAiGame: I'll set the AI to its weakest level. If you get lost, you can peek at the board.
script.readyPractice: You'll see a name like "e4" — tap that square. There's no time limit.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
howToPlay.body: Find the symmetrical square on the board for the given symmetry type.

step_intro.title: What is Board Symmetry?
step_intro.body: Training board symmetry helps you instantly find corresponding squares. There are three main types of symmetry on the chessboard.

step_horizontal.title: Vertical Symmetry (File)
step_horizontal.body: Squares symmetric with respect to the central vertical line (between d and e files). Example: a1 ↔ h1, c3 ↔ f3.

step_vertical.title: Horizontal Symmetry (Rank)
step_vertical.body: Squares symmetric with respect to the central horizontal line (between 4th and 5th ranks). Example: a1 ↔ a8, h2 ↔ h7.

step_point.title: Point Symmetry (Center)
step_point.body: Squares symmetric with respect to the center of the board (rotated 180 degrees). Example: a1 ↔ h8, c3 ↔ f6.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
howToPlay.body: Questions like the following will be asked repeatedly. Identify whether the given square is light or dark.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
howToPlay.body: Identify the two diagonals that pass through the given square.

step_diagonal.title: What is a Diagonal?
step_diagonal.body:
A diagonal runs in the a1-h8 direction.
All squares where (file - rank) is constant belong to the same diagonal.
The green squares show the diagonal passing through d4.

step_antiDiagonal.title: What is an Anti-diagonal?
step_antiDiagonal.body:
An anti-diagonal runs in the h1-a8 direction.
All squares where (file + rank) is constant belong to the same anti-diagonal.
The blue squares show the anti-diagonal passing through d4.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
howToPlay.body: Calculate the shortest path for a piece to reach a target square.

step_intro.title: The Objective
step_intro.body: Find the shortest path for the Knight to move from Start (e4) to Target (h5).

step_visualization.title: Visualize the Route
step_visualization.body:
There is no board preview during practice. Visualize the path in your head and input the coordinates.
Example: e4 -> f6 -> h5

overview.title: What is the Knight's Tour?
overview.body:
A training exercise where you move a knight to visit all 64 squares exactly once.
It trains your sense of knight movement and board geometry, so keeping at it improves your visualization skills.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.body:
The Knight's Tour is a classic chess puzzle.

Using a knight, try to visit all 64 squares of the board exactly once.

about.title: Algebraic Notation

overview.title: What is FEN Reconstruction?
overview.body:
A training exercise where you read a FEN string and recreate the position on the board.
It trains your ability to turn notation into a mental image of the board, so keeping at it improves your visualization skills.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.body: Practice reading FEN notation and recreating board positions.

overview.title: What is Position Memory?
overview.body:
A training exercise where you recreate a position on the board.
It trains your pattern-recognition ability and working memory, so keeping at it improves your visualization skills.

Memorize a position within the time limit, then recreate it on an empty board.

criteria.5kyu: Ability to correctly identify the square on the chess board from algebraic notation (e.g., e4, Bg7).
criteria.4kyu: Ability to determine legal moves at a specified coordinate for all pieces without visual aids.
criteria.3kyu: Ability to plan piece maneuvering routes for all pieces without visual aids.
criteria.2kyu: Able to recognize multiple pieces as a single meaningful chunk.
criteria.1kyu: Being able to beat the engine under some blindfold constraint.
criteria.1dan: Being able to beat the engine at blindfold chess.
